newsitem.title: USA: General Dynamics buying two Lockheed units for $450 million.
newsitem.headline: General Dynamics buying two Lockheed units for $450 million.

text.p: General Dynamics Corp., continuing the expansion of its defence manufacturing businesses, said Thursday it agreed to pay about $450 million to acquire two units of Lockheed Martin Corp. that make combat vehicles and gun systems.
General Dynamics said the units were expected to produce some $500 million in revenues this year and "significantly higher" revenues in 1997 and would immediately add to its profits.

The company, which builds nuclear submarines, surface combat ships and armoured vehicles, said it was buying Lockheed Martin's armament systems unit, which has plants in Burlington, Vt. and Milan, Tenn., and its defence systems unit in Pittsfield, Mass.
The armament systems unit, which has some 1,600 employees, manufactures advanced gun, ammunition handling and air defence systems, and produces Gatling guns for air, land and sea-based applications.
The defence systems business, which employs about 1,650 people, builds turrets and transmissions for combat vehicles, and missile guidance and naval fire control systems.

The transaction, expected to close by the end of the year, marks the third major acquisition this year by General Dynamics, which is based in Falls Church, Va. The company also bought shipbuilder Bath Iron Works and Teledyne Vehicle Systems this year.
"Armament systems and defence systems are an excellent strategic fit with our organisation," General Dynamics Chairman James R. Mellor said in a statement.
"The acquisition expands our participation in armoured vehicles from heavy tanks to light vehicles, and from full platforms to major subsystems.

"Furthermore, the acquisition gives us for the first time a strategic position in turret, gun and ammunition systems for land, sea and air platforms, and widens our defence business base into ordnance and naval fire control systems."

Lockheed Martin Chief Executive Norman R. Augustine said the two units were both solid firms but outside Lockheed Martin's core business as it concentrates on larger scale electronic systems and systems integration work.
"The resulting lack of synergies will preclude these businesses from realising their full potential within Lockheed Martin," he said.
Lockheed Martin, based in Bethesda, Md., is a highly diversified advanced technology company that primarily manufactures electronics for military and civil applications.
General Dynamics said that as part of the purchase agreement it will recognise existing labour unions and honour all existing labour contracts at the two units.
It also said the transaction had been approved by the boards of both companies but was still subject to regulatory approvals.
General Dynamics's stock added $2 to $69.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange while Lockheed Martin's stock lost 25 cents to $90.125, also on the NYSE.
